profile.headline: MSCS @ UC San Diego
profile.summary: Hello, I’m Kevin Kim, an MSCS student at UC San Diego. Drawing on my neuroscience background, I build AI inspired by human cognition, especially metacognitive LLM multi-agent systems where agents track their own confidence and reliability. I’m now exploring agentic recommender systems as a setting for modeling human preferences.

positions.title: Visiting Researcher – Human-Centered AI
positions.description:
• Designed and ran a 7-condition reverse-sycophancy pilot testing whether user praise vs. criticism shifts LLM confidence, accuracy, and acceptance of valid corrections (MMLU-Pro, SuperGPQA-hard).
• Built a Python eval pipeline over 320+ conversations with Gemini and Claude (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus) scoring calibration and answer flips; extending to open models via Ollama with logprob confidence.
• Presenting and critiquing papers in a weekly seminar reading group; collaborating with peers on shared research directions.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Exploring novel multi-agent topologies aimed at giving LLM systems metacognitive capability, with the goal of improving performance on reasoning and cognitive task suites. 
• Implementing orchestration, inter-agent communication, and tool-calling interfaces in Python; comparing topology variants against single-agent baselines. 
• Extending evaluation to clinical agent benchmarks including MedAgentBench. 
• Writing literature reviews on multi-agent architectures and machine metacognition to situate the work against existing approaches.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
• Prototyped an LLM pipeline that turns clinical report templates and study source data into populated first drafts, with OCR ingestion of past reports and an eval harness scoring drafts against author-edited ground truth.
• Automated a preclinical study data package with T-SQL stored procedures pulling Provantis (Oracle) data over a linked server into a 14-tab SSRS report, replacing a hand-assembled Excel workbook.
• Interviewed report authors to scope the system; presented a build/no-build recommendation to leadership.

positions.title: Artificial Intelligence Research Fellow & Student Lead
positions.description:
• Built an NLP pipeline (DistilBERT + Rasch IRT) over 2,000 assessment and feedback records to evaluate Emory’s Chemistry Unbound curriculum, replacing a 50+ hour manual review per cycle.
• Engineered a stacked ensemble (XGBoost, MLP, CNN under an XGBoost meta-learner) on custom spatiotemporal features to predict explosive NFL run plays (0.71 AUC); built a Bayesian state-space model of latent kicker talent.
• TA for DATASCI 497R: mentored 30+ undergraduate researchers and taught Python/PyTorch workshops;
partnered with sponsors including Invest Atlanta.
positions.insights: Skills: Python (Programming Language) · Data Engineering · Research Skills

positions.title: Health Economics Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Compiled data concerning mental health insurance payments to study mental health provider reimbursement rates and conducted research on nationwide mental health parity law databases
• Written reports and literature reviews on topics such as closing of the Wellstar Medical Center
• Built various statistical econometric models leveraging national databases such as MEPS or AHRF data to explore various issues in mental health access inequality

positions.title: Oncology Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Led qualitative analysis using Dedoose to help architect a web-based intervention for psychoneurological symptoms of colorectal cancer patients after screening dozens of patients and collecting/entering data
• Co-authored a study published in Cancer Nursing (internationally recognized medical journal) on the web-based intervention we had developed

organizations.position: High School Volunteer / Event Team Leader · Aug 2018 - Jun 2022
organizations.description: As a High School Volunteer at SVKS, I help instructors instruct and construct interactive lesson plans to educate youth on the Korean Language and Korean Culture with an accumulated 350+ volunteering hours. In the event team, I hold a leadership role that coordinates the planning and materials needed for events that SVKS are involved in.
